s: A company has several Amazon DynamoDB tables in an AWS Region. Each table has more than 100,000 records and was created with default table settings. To reduce costs, the company needs to identify unused tables. However, the company must maintain the availability and current performance capability of the tables in case the company must use the tables in the future. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)
o: In Amazon CloudWatch, graph the sum of the ReadThrottleEvents metric and the sum of the WriteThrottleEvents metric for each table over a period of 1 month.
In Amazon CloudWatch, graph the sum of the ConsumedReadCapacityUnits metric and the sum of the ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits metric for each table over a period of 1 month.
Change the provisioned RCUs to 1 for the unused tables. Change the provisioned WCUs to 1 for the unused tables.
Change the capacity mode of the unused tables to on-demand mode.
Change the table class of the unused tables to DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA).
Purchase a reserved capacity of 1 RCU and 1 WCU for each unused table.

w.y: Tables with near-zero ConsumedReadCapacityUnits and ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits over a month are unused. Switching them to on-demand removes idle provisioned-capacity charges while keeping their ability to serve traffic instantly. The DynamoDB Standard-IA table class cuts storage cost for rarely accessed data without changing availability or performance.

o.A: Throttle events show capacity shortfalls, not whether a table is used; an idle table shows zero throttles just like a well-sized busy one.
o.B: Correct: consumed RCU and WCU sums over a month show which tables get no traffic.
o.C: Setting 1 RCU and 1 WCU cuts the tables' performance capability, which breaks the requirement.
o.D: Correct: on-demand charges per request, so idle tables cost almost nothing for throughput and still scale if used.
o.E: Correct: Standard-IA lowers storage price for infrequently accessed tables with the same availability and performance.
o.F: Reserved capacity is a commitment for steady provisioned use; buying it for unused tables adds cost, and the minimum purchase is 100 units.

s: Evaluate your DynamoDB table's capacity mode
